scope: Native RTX 4090 installer: lab IPv4 listener, browser origin and TLS setup

automated_tests.command: PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/bin:$PATH TMPDIR=/private/tmp uv run --python 3.12 --no-project python -m unittest discover -s scripts/onprem -q
covers: Resume without prompting or changing recorded listener and certificate mode
Reject invalid URLs, bind-address injection and public ACME for private IPv4
Actual OpenSSL 3 certificate/key/SAN/expiry and CA PEM validation
Reject wrong host, mismatched key and invalid CA without overwriting saved material
Read-only Kubernetes Secret mount readable by nonroot gateway group
Export only public CA and reject a changed recorded CA
Use explicitly trusted TLS client for S3 PUT/GET/Range checks

isolated_runtime_probe.runtime: Docker, separate containers; no VideoQ application or Kubernetes changes
isolated_runtime_probe.client: curl --cacert with --connect-to; certificate and hostname verification enabled
isolated_runtime_probe.provided_startup: One transient TLS EOF before the gateway finished loading; retry succeeded

limitations: A fresh lab machine installation and lab firewall/DNS configuration were not exercised
Trust-store enrollment on end-user PCs remains an administrator task
Supplied certificates require renewal by their issuer and installer rerun
Binding an IP does not assign it to a NIC or restrict client source networks
The existing shared-IP Vast instance remains on its previous browser origin

checked: No network prompts with a single LAN address
Exclude container bridges, VPN and link-local interfaces; prefer private IPv4
Ask for IP only when multiple candidates exist; manual URL fallback when none
Resume preserves saved URL and legacy ACME settings
Actual Ubuntu VM detection returned ens3 IPv4 and excluded bridge/VPN interfaces
